originality.rationale: A sharp additive change bound for Pianka overlap under merging two resource categories was checked against the original Pianka cosine-index definition, ecological categorical-data/full-text treatments and modern implementer documentation; relevant published mathematical result queries returned no same or stronger conclusion. The theorem is not implied merely by formula definitions, alternative compositional indices, or the observation that grouping is problematic. An equivalent nonnegative-vector angular-distortion inequality elsewhere remains a specific unresolved bibliographic risk; independent review is not represented as complete.
residual_risks: The full mathematical bodies of Hurlbert (1978), Abrams (1980) and Slobodchikoff–Schulz (1980) were not available; an exact earlier result cannot be excluded.
General positive-cone angular-distortion or cosine similarity literature outside ecological indexing may imply the same sharp constant; targeted searches were not an exhaustive bibliography.
The full 22-page scanned Pianka (1973) paper was not read sequentially; the defining formula and immediately relevant resource-use methods were inspected.
No independent review of originality or proof was conducted.

value.rationale: Resource classes in empirical diet/habitat surveys are routinely pooled, making one-step resolution stability of a classical descriptive overlap coefficient a concrete mathematical calibration problem. The result gives the best possible dimension-independent 0.132514... downward envelope, exact attaining support pattern, upward change 1 and a structurally contrasting monotone Schoener index; it does not claim to infer competition or sampling bias.
